text:
Amy - sales: Heads-up: New timeline from AcmeCorp. They want a one-week Private POC in their AWS account. Security mandates outbound TLS inspection and strict allowlist. They also asked whether we can: 1) preserve original client IPs for logging/billing, 2) provide a small set of static egress IPs, and 3) supply a short GRC blurb about KMS/audit logs.

Sandeep - solutions: Quick reality check: If traffic exits via their TLS-inspecting proxy, the proxy terminates TLS and opens a new connection -> client src IP is replaced by proxy IP. Two realistic approaches:
- Customer keeps NAT with static EIP and we route to the internet via their NAT (peering/transit) -> static egress controlled by customer, but no TLS inspection on that path.
- Customer proxy stays in path -> we see proxy IP; to recover client identity we need the proxy to inject X-Forwarded-For or PROXY protocol and for us to trust it. That still doesn't guarantee network-level srcip preservation.

Olivia - netops: Deployment options we can offer for an AWS Private POC:
- VPC Peering / Transit Gateway route into customer VPC. Customer owns NAT Gateway + EIP(s). Pros: they control egress & allowlisting; cons: vendor must accept no TLS-bump on the egress path for model pulls.
- Interface VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink) to their proxy endpoint. Our connector tunnels to that ENI and the proxy handles egress. Pros: fits strict outbound inspection; cons: we cannot preserve original src IP unless proxy adds proxy-protocol/XFF and doesn't re-nat later.
- Run a lightweight forward-proxy inside customer VPC (managed by Redwood). We assign a small EIP pool to it and we control egress IPs for allowlisting; cons: operator access and governance conversations required.

Jordan - eng: Technical caveats:
- TLS-inspection will break cert pinning and mTLS. If they require mTLS to model repositories, we need certificate exchange or a passthrough.
- Websockets/long-lived streams: MTU and TLS-bump interplay can cause disconnects; recommend enabling TCP keepalive and monitor jitter.

Marta - security: Proposed GRC blurb they can paste: 
"Redwood Private POC (summary): Data plane runs inside customer-owned VPC. Customers retain NSG/NACL control and can restrict egress. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and offers HSM-backed key options for enterprise. Per-request audit logs (request id, timestamp, model id, route) are available and can be exported to customer S3 or SIEM."

Amy - sales: Nice. They also need a minimal firewall allowlist for their network team. Keep it tight.

Sandeep - solutions: Minimal POC allowlist suggestion:
- TCP 443 -> Redwood control plane, model APIs, artifact endpoints
- TCP 80 -> redirections (optional)
- UDP/TCP 53 -> DNS or provide conditional forwarder to our resolvers
- UDP 123 -> NTP (if they block time sync)
- TCP 5228-5240 -> gRPC/streaming (only if using streaming features)
Note: If traffic goes via their TLS-proxy, ensure SNI is not rewritten and proxy supports forwarding SNI for routing.

Olivia - netops: For preserving client identity in logs: ask if their proxy supports PROXY protocol v1/v2 or consistent X-Forwarded-For insertion without subsequent NAT. We can accept PROXY protocol on our connector and ingest the original IP into logs (not as L3 srcip).

Jordan - eng: Also request they allow specific storage endpoints for artifact pulls (S3/GCS) or pre-stage images in their account. That avoids extra egress complexity during the POC.

support-bot: Created ticket POC-7899 and attached notes.

Amy - sales: Thanks team. Action items: Sandeep/Jordan paste the GRC blurb and allowlist into POC-7899. Olivia to draft the three deployment options as a 1-page handoff. I'll confirm whether Acme will enable PROXY protocol/XFF or prefer our managed forwarder.

Sandeep - solutions: Will update ticket by EOD. If they ask about pricing for managed forwarder/EIP pool, estimate: small POC (1-2 vCPUs proxy) add-on ~$600/week + EIP cost per AWS pricing.

Marta - security: If we accept PROXY protocol, include requirement for TLS certificate pin exceptions and controls in the contract.

Amy - sales: Perfect:thumbsup:
